Let none of you be drunk or quarrelsome, for it is not fitting for the servant of the Lord to quarrel. Let no one carry weapons during a disturbance, because our weapons ought to be spiritual. Let no one devote himself to games involving dogs or birds. Do not drink in taverns.

Let each of you announce to his people on Sunday or feast days as much of the Gospel or the Apostle as he understands. You must preach the word of the Lord. Care for the poor, strangers, and orphans, and invite them to your meal. Be hospitable, so that others may take a good example from you.

Every Sunday, before Mass, make holy water with which the people may be sprinkled, and have a vessel for this purpose alone. Do not give sacred vessels or priestly vestments as pledges to a merchant or tavernkeeper.

Let none of you bring a penitent who is unworthy, for whatever reason, to reconciliation, or give him a certificate of reconciliation. Let none of you demand interest or become the tenant of his superior.

Know that the goods and possessions you acquire after the day of your ordination belong to the church to which you are titled. Let no one acquire a church without our knowledge and consent. Let no one obtain a church through the power of secular authorities. Let no one supplant another in a church by means of money. Let no one leave the church to which he is titled and move to another for the sake of gain.

Let no one hold several churches without the assistance of other priests. Under no circumstances is one church to be divided among several persons. Let no one receive another’s parishioner for Mass except while he is traveling or if the matter has been arranged there. Let no one sing Mass in another’s parish without the will and request of its own priest.

Let no one receive a tithe belonging to another. Let no one invite a penitent to eat meat or drink wine unless he gives alms for him at that time. Let no one presume to baptize except on the vigils of Easter and Pentecost, unless there is danger of death.

Each of you should have a stone baptismal font. If he cannot have one made of stone, he should have another vessel prepared for this purpose, in which nothing else is done. Take care to teach all your parishioners the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer.

Make it known to your people that the fasts of the Four Ember Seasons, the Rogations, and the Greater Litany must be observed in every way. On the Wednesday before Lent, invite the people to confession, and impose penance upon them according to the character of their offense—not according to your own judgment, but as it is written in the penitential book.

Three times a year—that is, at Christmas, Easter, and Pentecost—admonish all the faithful to approach Communion of the body and blood of the Lord. Exhort married people to abstain from their wives at appointed times.

Distribute eulogies to the people after Mass on feast days. Let no priest travel without an orarium or stole. Let none of you wear lay clothing. Let no one presume to sell, exchange, or alienate by any means any object, possession, or slave belonging to the church.

Teach the people to celebrate Sunday and the other festivals without servile labor, from vespers to vespers. Prohibit the singing and dancing of women in the churchyard. Under solemn adjuration by Almighty God, forbid the devilish songs that the common people customarily perform over the dead during the night, as well as the laughter they practice.

Do not communicate with excommunicated persons. Let no one presume to sing Mass for them. Announce this also to the peoples entrusted to you. Let none of you attend weddings. Announce to everyone that no one may take a wife except at a publicly celebrated wedding.

Forbid abduction in every way, and forbid anyone to approach his nearest blood relative or take another man’s betrothed. Make swineherds and other shepherds come to Mass, at least on Sunday.

Let godparents teach their godchildren, or have them taught, the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer. Always keep the chrism under lock or seal because of certain unfaithful persons.

We wish to know of every priest whether he was born of free parents or of servile condition, whether he was born or ordained in our parish or in another, and to what place he has been previously titled. If he was a slave, let him produce his charter of freedom. If he is from another parish, let him produce letters of recommendation, which are called a *formata*.

We also wish to admonish you concerning the ministry entrusted to you: each of you, if possible, should keep with him a written exposition of the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer according to the tradition of the orthodox Fathers, understand it completely, and diligently instruct the people entrusted to him by preaching it. If he cannot do this, let him at least retain it in memory or believe it.

He should also understand well the prayers of the Mass, the Prefaces, and the Canon. If he cannot, let him at least be able to recite them distinctly and from memory. He should be able to read the Epistle and Gospel well; and would that he could at least explain their meaning literally.

He should know how to pronounce the words and divisions of the Psalms regularly from memory, together with the customary canticles. He must know by heart the sermon of Bishop Athanasius on the faith of the holy Trinity, which begins, “Whoever wishes,” and sing it every day.

He must be able and know how to recite distinctly, in the plural and singular forms as appropriate, the exorcisms and prayers for making a catechumen, for consecrating the font, and the remaining prayers over a male and a female. Likewise, he must know the order for baptizing and for assisting the sick.

He should at least know how to read correctly the order for reconciling penitents according to the manner canonically reserved to him, the order for anointing the sick, and the prayers appropriate to that need. Likewise, he should know the order and prayers for funerals and for the rites performed for the dead.

He must likewise know by heart the exorcisms and blessings of salt and water. He should know the nocturnal and daytime chant. If he cannot master the greater computation, he should at least know the lesser: the epacts, concurrent cycles, regulars, the Paschal terms, and the other elements, if possible.

Let him possess a Martyrology and a Penitential, so that, according to what is written there, he may question the person confessing or impose the appropriate manner of penance upon one who has confessed. Let each of you possess this little book and read it frequently, lest he forget what he is required to observe.

Now, dearest brothers, may Almighty God grant that you be able, insofar as human weakness permits, to fulfill by good works what you have received through our tradition, and to retain it in memory and carry it out beneficially. His kingdom and dominion remain without end, forever and ever. Amen. [Col. 0456B–0458B]

### III. NEW SYNODAL ADMONITION, WHICH WAS READ AFTER THE GOSPEL BY THE BISHOP SEATED IN THE FALDISTORIUM

From the *Roman Pontifical* of Augustinus Patricius de Picolominibus, bishop of Pienza.

Dearest brothers, fellow priests and co-workers in our order: let your fraternity know that we, although unworthy, occupy the place of Aaron, while you occupy that of Eleazar and Ithamar. We act in the place of the twelve apostles, while you represent the seventy-two disciples. We are your shepherds, while you are shepherds of the souls entrusted to you. We shall render an account of you to our Lord Jesus Christ, while you shall render an account of the peoples entrusted to your care.

Therefore, so that on the day of the fearful judgment we may be found among the good stewards, we admonish and beseech your fraternity that your life and conduct be irreproachable. Women must not live together with you in your houses. Rise every night for the nocturnal hours. Sing your office at the appointed hours.

Celebrate Mass only while fasting, and prepared not in ordinary clothing but in sacred vestments: amice, alb, cincture, maniple, stole, and chasuble. These vestments must be clean and not used for other purposes. Celebrate devoutly and reverently, and at Mass receive the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ with all reverence and trembling.

Corporals and palls must be made of linen and be perfectly clean. Wash and carefully wipe them, together with the other linens and sacred vessels, with your own hands. The altar must be covered with clean linens, at least three separate ones, and no woman may approach it.

Nothing may be placed upon it except relics, sacred objects, and things suitable for the sacrifice. Your Missals, Graduals, Lectionaries, and Antiphonaries must be complete and in good order.

Your churches must be well roofed and clean. In the sacristies or secretaries, or near the high altar, there must be a suitable place for pouring out the water used to wash the corporals, linens, vessels, and other sacred objects, as well as the hands after you have handled the holy chrism or the oil of catechumens or the sick.

A vessel containing clean water must hang there for washing the hands of priests and others who are about to perform a sacred act or divine office, and a clean cloth must be nearby for wiping them.

The churchyards must be well secured. Let no one obtain a church through secular power without our knowledge and consent. Let no one leave the church to which he has been titled and transfer to another for the sake of gain. Let no one presume to acquire several churches without a title and contrary to the provisions of the sacred canons.

Under no circumstances may one church be divided among several people. Let no one celebrate outside the church in unconsecrated places, or while wearing spurs, or with knives hanging visibly outside his clothing.

Let no one receive another’s parishioner for Communion except a traveler, and then only with the permission of his own rector. Let no one celebrate Mass in another’s parish without the permission of its own priest.

During the celebration, each person must sign the chalice and the offerings with the sign of the cross—not with a circular motion or wavering of the fingers, as some do, but with joined and extended fingers—and thus bless them.

The chalice and paten must be of gold or silver, not of bronze, brass, glass, or wood. Each priest must have a cleric or student who sings psalms with him, reads the Epistle and lesson, and answers at Mass.

The priest himself must visit and reconcile the sick, give them Communion with his own hand according to the Apostle, and anoint them with holy oil. Let no one presume to give Communion to a layman or woman to carry to a sick person.

Let no one demand a payment or gift for baptizing infants, reconciling adults or the sick, or burying the dead. Through your negligence, let no infant die without baptism or adult without Communion.

Let none of you be drunk or quarrelsome. Let no one carry weapons. Let no one devote himself to games involving dogs or birds, or drink in taverns.

Let each of you announce to his people as much of the Gospel as he understands on Sunday and the other feast days. Preach the word of the Lord. Care for the poor, strangers, widows, and orphans, and invite the strangers to your meal. Be hospitable, thereby providing others with a good example.

Every Sunday, before Mass, bless water with which the people may be sprinkled; have a vessel for this purpose alone.

Do not give sacred vessels or priestly vestments as pledges to a merchant or tavernkeeper. Do not bring an unworthy penitent to reconciliation for any reason, nor give him a certificate of reconciliation.

Do not exact interest. Do not alienate the goods you acquired after your ordination, because they belong to the church. No one may sell, exchange, or alienate by any means any object, possession, or slave belonging to the church.

Let no one receive another’s tithe. Let no one invite a penitent to eat meat or drink wine unless he gives alms for him at that time.

Each of you must have clean stone baptismal fonts. If he cannot have stone fonts, let him keep another vessel assigned solely to this purpose.

Teach all your parishioners the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer, and make known that the fasts of the Four Ember Seasons and the other commands of the Church must be observed.

On the Wednesday before Lent, admonish the people to confess, and impose penance upon those who confess according to the character of their offense. Three times a year—that is, at Christmas, Easter, and Pentecost—invite all the faithful to approach Communion of the body of our Lord Jesus Christ, and see to it that they communicate at least at Easter.

Exhort married people to abstain from their wives at appointed times. Let none of you wear red or green clothing, or lay clothing.

Teach the people to celebrate Sunday and the other festivals without servile labor, from vespers to vespers. Prohibit the songs and dances of women in the churchyard. Under solemn adjuration by Almighty God, forbid the incantations that the common people customarily perform over the dead during the night.

Do not communicate with excommunicated persons, and let none of you presume to celebrate for them or in their presence. Announce this also to the people. Let no one from the people take a wife into his household unless the wedding has first been publicly celebrated at a time permitted by the Church.

Forbid everyone to approach a woman who has been abducted or a blood relative, or to take another man’s betrothed. Have swineherds and other shepherds summoned to Mass at least on Sunday.

Exhort godparents to teach their godchildren, or have them taught, the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer. [Col. 0458C–0460A]

Carefully preserve the sacrament of the Eucharist, the holy chrism, the oil of catechumens, and the holy oil, or oil of the sick, in the church, in a clean, suitable, and secure place, under sacred and trustworthy custody.

Each of you must keep with him an exposition of the Creed and the Lord’s Prayer according to the traditions of the orthodox Fathers, and must understand them, as well as the prayers of the Mass, the Epistles, the Gospels, and the Canon. From these, by preaching, he must diligently instruct the people entrusted to him, especially those who do not believe correctly.

He must recite the Introit of the Mass, the prayers, the Epistle, the Gradual, the Gospel, the Creed, and the other non-secret prayers in a loud and intelligible voice. He must read the Secrets and the Canon slowly and distinctly in a subdued voice.

He must pronounce the words and divisions of the Psalms regularly and intelligibly, together with the customary canticles. He must know by heart the Creed of Athanasius concerning the Trinity and the Catholic faith.

He must distinctly recite, in the plural or singular as appropriate, the exorcisms and prayers for making catechumens and the remaining prayers over a male and a female. He must observe according to the canonical form the order for baptizing, assisting the sick, reconciliation, commending the soul, and conducting the funeral rites of the dead.

He must read the exorcisms and blessings of salt and water correctly. He must know the daytime and nocturnal chant. He must also know the lesser computation for finding the Sunday letter, the interval of the day of Easter, and the dates of the principal movable feasts.

Thus, together with the people entrusted to you, may you enjoy everlasting blessedness through these and other good works, with the help of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, belong honor and glory forever and ever. [Col. 0460B]

### IV. MOST RECENT SYNODAL ADMONITION, TO BE READ BY THE BISHOP AFTER THE GOSPEL

From the *Roman Pontifical*.

Dearest brothers and priests of the Lord, you are co-workers in our order. We, although unworthy, occupy the place of Aaron, while you occupy the place of Eleazar and Ithamar. We act in the place of the twelve apostles, while you represent the seventy-two disciples. We are your shepherds, while you are shepherds of the souls entrusted to you. We shall render an account of you to the supreme Shepherd, our Lord Jesus Christ, while you shall render an account of the peoples entrusted to your care.

Therefore, dearest brothers, consider your danger. Accordingly, we admonish and beseech your fraternity to commit to memory what we suggest to you and to strive to put it into practice.

First of all, we admonish you that your life and conduct be irreproachable. Women must not live together with you in your houses. Rise every night for the nocturnal hours. Sing your office at the appointed hours.

Let no one celebrate Mass unless he is fasting, and let him not wear ordinary clothing but sacred, clean vestments: amice, alb, cincture, maniple, stole, and chasuble, which must not be used for other purposes. Celebrate Mass reverently. Receive the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ with all reverence and trembling.
